subject: Mental Models
title: Kelly Criterion
description: A micro-lesson that makes Kelly Criterion usable.

hook.text: A gambler knows the odds favor him. Should he bet everything? Absolutely not. The size of the bet matters as much.

buildup.text: The Kelly Criterion tells you the optimal fraction of your bankroll to bet based on your edge and the odds offered.

discovery.text: John Larry Kelly Jr. developed this formula in 1956 at Bell Labs. It maximizes long-term wealth growth mathematically.

climax.text: Size your bets proportionally to your edge. Overbetting destroys wealth even when the odds are in your favor.

punchline.text: Even with good odds, bet size determines survival.

quiz.question: What does the Kelly Criterion determine?
options: The optimal fraction of wealth to bet
The expected value of a gamble
